title: [Chapitre] VI. Analysis situs (deuxième mouture) : notes manuscrites (18-20/06/1986).

deep.reconstruction:
Setting: the 1986 'Analysis situs' notes develop an axiomatic theory of 'pieces' (objects of a 'multiplicity' M) with three relations: inclusion (⊂, ≤), refinement (X' ≪ X, X' is a refinement or subdivision of X), and compatibility (≬). Operations include restriction of a refinement to a subpiece (X'|Y), intersection (∩), union or gluing (∪) and join of refinements (∨), governed by numbered axioms (Ax 4, a gluing axiom, At 9–12).

Page 74 sets up H = F ∪ G with K = F ∩ G. It shows that a refinement H' ≪ H induces a 'cube' diagram: refinements F' = H'|F, G' = H'|G and H'_K, together with the restrictions F'_K = F'|K and G'_K = G'|K. All horizontal squares are cartesian and cocartesian.

Page 75 proves the converse, i.e. the gluing of refinements along a union. Suppose F' ≪ F and G' ≪ G are given, and their restrictions F'_K and G'_K to K are compatible.
1. Put H'_K = F'_K ∨ G'_K, the common refinement. By Ax 4, H'_K ≪ K. Also K' = F'_K ∩ G'_K.
2. Now regard F' (a refinement of F) and H'_K (a refinement of K ⊂ F). By construction F'_K ≤ H'_K, i.e. H'_K is finer than the restriction of F' to K.
3. Suppose one could show that such a pair is compatible. Then one could form their union H'_F ≪ F, and symmetrically H'_G ≪ G, built from G' and H'_K.
4. One checks directly that H'_F|K = H'_K = H'_G|K.
5. The gluing axiom then gives H'_F ≬ H'_G, and H' = H'_F ∪ H'_G is a refinement of H restricting to the given data.

Hence the non-trivial part of the proposition reduces to the special case G ⊂ F with F'|G ≤ G'. That case is stated on p.76 as 'Cor. Main': if G ≤ F, F' ≪ F and G' ≪ G is finer than F'|G, then F' and G' are compatible (and F' ∩ G' = F'_G). Equivalently, a refinement of a subpiece that is finer than the induced refinement extends to a refinement of the whole piece.

This is the axiomatic analogue of a classical fact of PL topology: a subdivision of a subcomplex extends to a subdivision of the whole complex. Grothendieck then asks (p.76) whether it follows from the other axioms, and recasts it as the axiom At 11'/At 12.
errors: No outright error. The step 'on vérifierait sans mal H'_F|K = H'_K' is asserted, not proved; it relies on unstated properties of restriction of a union of compatible refinements.
The key compatibility of F' with H'_K is explicitly left open (conditional 'si...'). It is then isolated as Cor. Main / a new axiom on the next page, so the page itself proves only a reduction.

ideas.what: Gluing of refinements over a union H = F ∪ G: refinements of F and G that are compatible on K = F ∩ G glue to a refinement of H (converse of the cube diagram on p.74).
ideas.modern_name: Mayer–Vietoris / sheaf-like gluing property of subdivisions (refinements form a 'sheaf of posets' over the pieces)
ideas.usually_credited_to: classical PL topology (Whitehead, Zeeman; Rourke–Sanderson textbook treatment)
ideas.where_published: Only allusively: Esquisse d'un programme §5–6 on 'topologie modérée'; the axiomatics here are unpublished

ideas.what: Reduction to the extension case: a refinement of a subpiece finer than the induced one extends to a compatible refinement of the ambient piece.
ideas.modern_name: Extension of subdivisions from a subcomplex (PL topology); refinement of cell decompositions or stratifications compatible with a subset (o-minimal geometry)
ideas.usually_credited_to: standard PL topology; for o-minimal structures, van den Dries

ideas.what: Axiomatic framework of 'multiplicités' of pieces with relations ⊂, ≪ (refinement), ≬ (compatibility), and operations ∨, ∩, ∪, restriction, plus a gluing axiom.
ideas.modern_name: Axiomatic tame topology / abstract theory of dévissages (cf. o-minimal structures, Shiota's tame sets)
ideas.usually_credited_to: o-minimality: van den Dries, Pillay–Steinhorn, Knight

missed.claim: Grothendieck isolates the extension property (Cor. Main / At 11', At 12) as the crux of gluing refinements. On the next page he asks whether it follows from his other axioms or must be added. The question of a minimal axiom set for tame refinement theories appears not to have been settled in his notes or in the literature.
missed.quote: pour vérifier la partie non triviale de la proposition, on est ramené au cas particulier où G ⊂ F et où F'_G ≤ G'
missed.why_it_might_matter_today: Minor interest for anyone formalizing an axiomatic 'tame topology' that is independent of o-minimality. Mathematically, the content is standard in PL and o-minimal settings.

deep.surprise_reason: A routine sheaf-style reduction inside Grothendieck's unpublished axiomatics of tame spaces. The underlying fact (extending subdivisions from a subcomplex) is classical; only the axiomatic framework itself is of historical interest.
transcription_corrections: Line 'Si pour ces conditions qu'ils sont compatibles' is probably 'Dire [ou: si l'on savait] qu'ils sont compatibles, ...': a conditional meaning 'if we knew they are compatible, we could construct their union'.
In '(… de G' et de H'_K)' the struck word before 'de G'' is likely 'réunion' or 'recollement', i.e. H'_G is the union of G' and H'_K.
'on saurait H'_F ≬ H'_G' should be read as 'on saurait que H'_F ≬ H'_G'.
Final line: under G ⊂ F the double arrows point to G' and F' respectively (refinements), and the condition reads F'_G ≤ G'.
